2027 Kia Sorento HEV Drops With a $39,090 Price Tag, Undercuts Honda Pilot
10 photos
Photo: Kia
Kia has just revealed pricing for its new 2027 Sorento HEV, and the configurator went live with new tech features and optional blackout exterior elements for the one below it. Kia’s mid-size SUV undercuts the Honda Pilot and Mazda CX-90, but arrives more expensive than its brother from another mother, the Hyundai Santa Fe.
The 2027 Kia Sorento HEV arrives in America with a starting price of $39,090. For the money, customers get the base trim, the Sorento HEV EX with front-wheel drive. Those who want to go home with a Sorento HEV X-Line EX with all-wheel drive will pay $1,800 more.
Regardless of the traction wheels, the base trim gets an eight-way power-adjustable driver’s seat, heated front seats, the 12.3-inch touchscreen with navigation, a six-speaker audio system, the seven-seat layout, and the Smart Power Liftgate.
Upper in the range sits the Kia Sorento HEV X-Line EX, which is a $43,090 deal. This version is available with all-wheel drive only. For the money, buyers get the new blackout exterior design elements, along with matching gloss-black wheels and premium machined wood inlays inside the cabin.
Photo: Kia A panoramic sunroof, the SynTex seat upholstery, and second-row Captain's Chairs are also on board Kia’s all-new midsize SUV, while the Bose Premium Audio provides the soundtrack inside the cabin.
The Sorento HEV X-Line SX-Prestige sits at the top of the lineup, expectedly with the highest price: it starts at $47,590. The range-topping version comes with the 360-degree Surround View Monitor and Navigation-Based Smart Cruise Control with Stop & Go.
The driver gets a 14-way power seat with memory, four-way power lumbar adjustment, and two-way power thigh extension, along with aluminum sport pedals. Leather upholstery and a heated second row are also on board. The range-topping SX-Prestige also gains a standard Head-Up Display, while it is not available on the lower EX or X-Line EX trims.
The "HEV" lettering shows up on the tailgate, while the Sorento lineup ditches the old Steel Gray exterior paint in favor of the new Pale Gray, which can be selected at no extra cost. In the meantime, the Premium Paint options cost $495.
Photo: Kia Regardless of the trim, the 2027 Kia Sorento HEV retains the already familiar setup, which integrates the 1.6-liter inline-four turbocharged gas engine with direct injection, paired with a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor. Together, they produce 227 horsepower (230 metric horsepower) and 258 pound-feet (350 Newton meters) of torque.
The front-wheel-drive entry-level variant does 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 7.2 seconds. Because they are heavier, the all-wheel-drive variants need roughly half a second more, which is still impressive for the midsize SUV segment. Top speed is electronically limited at 120 mph (193 kph).
Kia also offers a cheaper and a more expensive Sorento in the United States. The base Sorento comes with a 2.5-liter, zero electrification, and 191 horsepower (194 metric horsepower) for a starting price of $32,590.
In the meantime, the Sorento Plug-in Hybrid with the 1.6-liter turbocharged inline-four and an electric motor for 261 horsepower (268 metric horsepower) will set you back $48,290.
